recommendation_summary: Action now: keep the shared folder for drafts only. On approval, a reviewer who is not the author saves the exact approved file into a separate archive that blocks changes and deletion for seven years, and that version carries the reviewer's authenticated identity and the system approval time. No optional additions are offered. Unmet need: the user still has to confirm which archive or existing store can lock files for seven years before the agent sets up the release path.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The signed customer contract requires every released document to keep its exact approved version, the approver's identity, and the approval time for seven years; the approver must be someone other than the author; later edits must leave that approved version unchanged. You asked to keep the shared folder, add an APPROVED column of typed initials, and agree a naming convention for this week's delivery.
labels.Deleted: The initials column, the naming convention, and the author-editable folder as the approved record. Authors can change the file, the initials, and any time written there, so those three cannot hold the contract's proof.
labels.Bottleneck: A copy that stays fixed for seven years and is bound to an authenticated approver and a system timestamp, before this week's delivery.
labels.Checked myself: Your account of the contract, twelve remote authors, three reviewers, weekly releases, and author edit access to the current shared folder. I have not inspected the folder or the contract.

note: The reply picks an archive that blocks changes, records a non-author approver with an authenticated identity and a system timestamp, and keeps the exact version for seven years; it also rejects the initials and naming-convention approach by name.
